correctness.rationale: The local tie-preserving minority fixed-point condition is opposite-neighbor count at least r. Binary window shifts yield exact closed-walk trace counts for every n>2r. Exact strongly connected component enumeration yields a sole primitive recurrent component of size 4,14,50,184 at respective radii. For each component a positive integer vector obtained by taking the fiftieth matrix power on the all-ones vector obeys strict componentwise rational Perron bounds, disjoint in precisely the claimed two-reversal order. The packaged stdlib Python implementation checks all exhaustive graph and integer assertions, and compares sixteen independent fixed-coloring enumerations with transfer traces. Finite experiments are only checks; the general trace/Perron argument is the proof.

value.rationale: A natural question is whether expanding a fixed symmetrical opposition neighborhood monotonically changes the abundance of locally stable antiferromagnetic states. The first four radii exhibit TWO direction reversals in the exponential count; this is not a parameter-renaming consequence of the known single-radius enumeration. The exact transfer identity provides all finite ring counts for these four dynamics, and the rational separation gives a reusable provable benchmark for studying competition radius.
